text: Ten-day period. A financial institution shall investigate promptly and determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error. It shall report the results to the consumer within three business days after completing its investigation and correct any error within one business day after determining one occurred.

Forty-five day period. If the institution cannot complete its investigation within 10 business days, it may take up to 45 days, provided it provisionally credits the consumer's account for the amount of the alleged error within 10 business days. It may withhold up to $50 if it has a reasonable basis for believing an unauthorized electronic fund transfer occurred.

Consumer liability for unauthorized electronic fund transfers. Liability is limited to $50 if the consumer notifies the institution within two business days of learning of the loss or theft, rises to as much as $500 if they fail to notify within two business days, and can be unlimited for transfers appearing on a periodic statement if not reported within 60 days.

Liability of cardholder for unauthorized use of a credit card is limited to the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained by the unauthorized use before the cardholder notified the card issuer. The issuer must have provided a means to identify the cardholder.

Billing error resolution for open-end credit. The consumer must give written notice of a billing error, including a charge they did not make or authorize, within 60 days after the first statement reflecting it. The creditor must acknowledge within 30 days and resolve within two billing cycles, not to exceed 90 days.

Visa dispute condition 10.4, Other Fraud Card-Absent Environment. Used when a cardholder states they did not authorize or participate in a card-not-present transaction. Issuer dispute time limit is generally 120 calendar days from the processing date. Merchant remedy requires compelling evidence the cardholder participated, such as prior matching transactions, delivery records, or device and address data.

Mastercard reason code 4837, No Cardholder Authorization. The cardholder states they did not authorize the transaction. Filing time limit is generally 120 calendar days. The merchant may remedy with evidence the cardholder authorized the purchase or that it continued an established relationship.

Unauthorized-charge procedure. Open a Reg E claim on the day of the call and start the 10-business-day clock. If the investigation cannot close within 10 business days, post provisional credit for the full disputed amount by business day 10 and notify the customer within 2 business days. Route any charge whose device fingerprint matches prior activity to fraud-ops for first-party review.

Approved disclosure for unauthorized-charge disputes. Tell the customer the dispute is opened and that written confirmation will arrive within 10 business days, that a provisional credit will be applied if the review runs past 10 days, and that the investigation completes within 45 days. Do not promise a final outcome and do not accuse the customer.

Consumer's right to stop payment of preauthorized transfers. A consumer may stop payment of a preauthorized recurring electronic fund transfer by notifying the financial institution orally or in writing at least three business days before the scheduled transfer date. The institution must honor the stop-payment order.

Visa dispute condition 13.2, Cancelled Recurring Transaction. The cardholder cancelled a subscription or recurring agreement but the merchant continued to bill the card. Time limit is generally 120 calendar days. Merchant remedy requires proof the cardholder did not cancel, or used the service after cancellation, or that the cancellation terms were not met.

Mastercard reason code 4841, Cancelled Recurring or Digital Goods Transactions. Applies when the cardholder was charged for a recurring subscription after cancelling it or after a free trial they did not convert. The merchant may remedy with evidence the cancellation was not valid or the service was provided.

Cancelled-subscription procedure. Capture the cancellation date and how the customer cancelled. For a debit card, place a stop-payment on the preauthorized recurring transfer under Reg E and block future debits from that merchant. Dispute the post-cancellation charges. For a credit card, file the billing-error dispute and request the merchant's cancellation evidence.

Approved phrasing for cancelled-subscription disputes. Confirm the cancellation date with the customer, tell them you will stop future recurring charges from that merchant and dispute the charges billed after cancellation. Ask whether they have a cancellation confirmation email. Do not tell the customer the charge is automatically valid because they used the service before.

Right of cardholder to assert claims and defenses. When goods or services purchased with a credit card are not delivered or not as agreed, the cardholder may assert against the card issuer the claims and defenses arising from the transaction, provided they made a good-faith attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant, subject to the $50 and geographic conditions.

Visa dispute condition 13.1, Merchandise or Services Not Received. The cardholder did not receive the goods or services by the agreed date or at all. Time limit is generally 120 calendar days from the expected delivery date. Merchant remedy requires proof of delivery or that the services were provided, such as tracking and a signature.

Mastercard reason code 4853, Cardholder Dispute, goods or services not provided. The cardholder paid but did not receive the purchased goods or services. The merchant may remedy with proof of delivery or fulfillment within the applicable filing window.

Goods-not-received procedure. Confirm the expected delivery or service date has passed. Record whether the customer attempted to resolve directly with the merchant, since networks and Reg Z claims-and-defenses generally expect a good-faith merchant attempt first. Capture the order number and expected delivery date, then file the dispute with the not-received reason code.

Approved phrasing for not-received disputes. Ask when the item or service was expected and whether the customer contacted the merchant. Tell them you will file a not-received dispute and that the merchant has a window to show proof of delivery. Do not promise the charge will be reversed before the investigation.

When a carrier cancels or significantly changes a flight to, from, or within the United States and the consumer does not accept rebooking or a voucher, the carrier must provide an automatic cash refund in the original form of payment within seven business days for credit-card purchases.

Timely notice given. If the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer’s liability for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, or a series of related unauthorized transfers, shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution.

Reassertion of error. A financial institution that has fully complied with the error-resolution requirements has no further responsibilities under this section should the consumer later reassert the same error, except in the case of an error the consumer reasserts following receipt of information provided in response to the original notice of error.
